headline: Coastal State Park Camping and Historic Village Stays
reservation: State park campsites at Russian Gulch and Van Damme require reservations through the official California State Parks portal, often six months out. Private glamping and historic village inns operate independently; distinguish between these and public land permits. Check the official site for current coastal access restrictions and seasonal closures.

days.title: Victorian Architecture and Headland Trails

stops.name: Mendocino Headlands State Park
stops.detail: Walk the bluffs surrounding the historic village to see sea arches and migrating whales in spring.

stops.name: Mendocino Coast Botanical Gardens
stops.detail: View heritage rhododendrons and succulents that thrive in the unique coastal microclimate.

days.driving: Allow 20 minutes for local coastal transit; conditions vary.
days.note: The village has narrow streets; parking is easier on the outskirts.

days.title: Redwoods and Sea Caves

stops.name: Van Damme State Park
stops.detail: Explore the Pygmy Forest where ancient trees remain stunted due to unique soil conditions.

stops.name: Russian Gulch State Park
stops.detail: Visit the 100-foot-wide 'Devil's Punchbowl' sinkhole and the iconic Pan-Pacific concrete arch bridge.

days.driving: Allow 30 minutes for Highway 1 transit; conditions vary.
days.note: Trails can be muddy; sturdy footwear is recommended for redwood canyons.

days.title: Glass Beaches and River Estuaries

stops.name: Glass Beach
stops.detail: Observe the smoothed sea glass remnants within MacKerricher State Park, part of the jagged coastline.

stops.name: Big River Estuary
stops.detail: Paddle or walk along the longest undeveloped estuary in Northern California for birdwatching.

days.driving: Allow 45 minutes for regional circuit; conditions vary.
days.note: Removing glass from the beach is prohibited by state law.

intel.title: Village and Trailhead Congestion
intel.text: Parking within the historic village is free but fills by noon on summer weekends. Use designated state park lots for bluff access to avoid local traffic bottlenecks.

intel.title: Coastal Dead Zones
intel.text: Signal is intermittent along Highway 1 between Santa Rosa and Mendocino. Use paper maps for navigation, especially when turning onto inland forest roads.

intel.title: Coastal Highway Pricing
intel.text: Fuel is available in Fort Bragg and Mendocino but is significantly more expensive than in Santa Rosa. Plan to fill up before departing the inland valleys.

intel.title: Marine Layer Visibility
intel.text: Summer morning fog (the 'marine layer') often obscures views until midday. Coastal hiking is often clearer and crisper during 'Indian Summer' in October.

intel.title: Tide Pool Safety
intel.text: Access to tide pools at MacKerricher is dependent on the tide cycle. Check local tide tables daily as rogue waves can occur regardless of the weather.

plan.arrival: Fly into Santa Rosa (STS) and pick up a rental car for the drive through Anderson Valley. Stop in Fort Bragg for larger grocery runs before checking into coastal inns.
plan.vehicle: A standard car is sufficient, but be prepared for winding, narrow stretches of Highway 1; check for road closures following heavy winter rains.
plan.goldenHour: Mendocino Headlands for sunset over the Pacific, dependent on daily fog conditions.
